children.description: Philodendron atabapoense is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron atratum Croat
children.description: Philodendron atratum ranges from southern Colombia (Putomayo) to southern Ecuador (Sucumbios, Napo, Pastaza, Morona-Santiago and Zamora-Chinchipe from 280-1524 m in a Premontane wet forest life zone. A single collection from Carchi Province on the Pacific slope in Tulcán Cantón appears to be this species also but since this would be the only species I know of from that area to occur in the Amazona basin, we are reserving judgment regarding its determination. A collection from Cajamarca Depart

children.name: Philodendron attenuatum Croat
children.description: Philodendron attenuatum is known from the Cordillera del Condor in southeastern Ecuador and northern to Central Peru (Amazonas, Loreto, Pasco). In Ecuador it ranges from Pastaza in the north to Zamora-Chinchipe.R. Rojas & G. Ortiz 5975 differs from Ecuadorian material of the species in having an arcuate sinus with no decurrent tissue along the petiole but otherwise must be placed in the species. J. Ruiz & J. Campos 1723 from the Peruvian province of San Martín in San Martín Province is probab

children.name: Philodendron aurantiifolium Schott
children.description: It ranges from extreme southeastern Chiapas to west-central Panama.

children.name: Philodendron aurantiispadix Croat
children.description: Philodendron aurantispadix is endemic to the type locality at La Planada at 1,700 to 1,850 m elevation in Premontane wet forest. It has been collected twice at La Planada, once along the trail to Pialapi, past the entrance to La Planada Field Station and once in a location not specifically known.

children.name: Philodendron aureimarginatum Croat
children.description: Philodendron aureimarginatum is most similar to P. wittianum Engl. a species with similar blade shape. That species differs in having shorter internodes, cataphylls that usually persist on the stem and blades that lack hyaline margins.

children.name: Philodendron auriculatum Standl. & L.O.Williams
children.description: Philodendron auriculatum is a flowering plant belonging to the genus Philodendron.

children.name: Philodendron auritum Lindl.
children.description: Guatemala (Although not included in Flora of Guatemala, 1958)

children.name: Philodendron auyantepuiense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Colombia, S. Venezuela to Guyana. It is a perennial or epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron avenium Grayum & Croat
children.description: It is characterized by finely ridged yellow-brown stems, nearly fully sheathed petioles, and oblong-elliptic, grayish-drying blades that lack obvious primary lateral veins on the dried blades.

children.name: Philodendron ayangannense Croat
children.description: The species is most similar to Philodendron hebetatum Croat from Central America and the western slopes of the Cordillera Occidental in Colombia and Ecuador but that species differs in having thicker glossy petioles with yellow-brown epidermis frequently loosened on drying, lower blade surfaces with distinctly visible minor veins and prominently visible laticifers, pale yellow-brown dried primary lateral veins (not darker as in P. ayangannense).

children.name: Philodendron azulitense Croat
children.description: Venezuela, known only from the type locality of La Azulita in the state of Merida.

children.name: Philodendron bahiense Engl.
children.description: Philodendron bahiense is a plant species endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron bakeri Croat & Grayum
children.description: Philodendron bakeri is a plant species native to Colombia, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama.

children.name: Philodendron balaoanum Engl.
children.description: Philodendron balaoanum is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron barbourii Croat
children.description: The species is characterized by long internodes, hemi-epiphytic habit, yellow-brown finely ridged dried stem, petioles about as long as the blades, and especially by the panduriform blades. Philodendron barbourii might be confused with P. panduriforme Schott, but that species has blades that are much broader and dry black. Philodendron barbourii is similar to

children.name: Philodendron barrosoanum G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, North Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron basii Matuda
children.description: Philodendron bazii is a plant species endemic to Mexico. The epithet is also spelt basii.

children.name: Philodendron basivaginatum K.Krause
children.description: Philodendron basivaginatum is a plant species endemic to Peru.

children.name: Philodendron baudoense Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron baudoense must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from many collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments.

children.name: Philodendron bayae Croat
children.description: Philodendron bayae is endemic to Colombia, known only from Chocó and Valle Departments at 40-150 m in a region of Tropical rain forest life zone or a transition zone between Tropical wet forest and Tropical rain forest life zones. The species was first collected by the senior author in 1984 in the Bajo Calima area and was subsequently collected four times in the same region and in 1997 by Croat & Gaskin in the region of Las Animas in Chocó Department.

children.name: Philodendron beniteziae Croat
children.description: Philodendron beniteziae ranges from Colombia (Antioquia, Choco, Narifio, Santander, Valle del Cauca), Ecuador (Carchi, Cotopaxi, Pichincha) to Venezuela (Tachira), at elevations of 1,600-2,060 m, in Premontane rain forest and Premontane wetforest.

children.name: Philodendron bernardoi Croat
children.description: Philodendron bernardoi is endemic to Colombia, known only from the type locality in Nariño Department at 1180 m in a Premontane rain forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron bernardopazii E.G.Gonç.
children.description: Philodendron bernardopazii is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to Espírito Santo in Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron bethoweniae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron bicolor Croat, Scherber., M.M.Mora & G.Ferry
children.description: The species is similar to Philodendron burlemarxii G. M. Barroso, which differs in having blades drying yellow-brown with less prominent primary lateral veins and with both blade surfaces short-pale-lineate, a more cordulate leaf base and less prominently long-acuminate blade apex as well as cataphylls which are acutely 2-ribbed.

children.name: Philodendron billietiae Croat
children.description: Philodendron billietiae is a hemi-epiphytic species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to Brazil, Guyana, and French Guiana.

children.name: Philodendron bipennifolium Schott
children.description: Philodendron bipennifolium is a plant species commonly known as the "fiddle-leaf philodendron".

children.name: Philodendron bipinnatifidum Schott ex Kunth, 1841
children.description: Philodendron bipinnatifidum, synonyms including Thaumatophyllum bipinnatifidum and Philodendron selloanum, (common names: split-leaf philodendron, lacy tree philodendron, selloum, horsehead philodendron, guaimbé) is a plant in the genus Philodendron, in the family Araceae. The species is native to South America, namely to Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, and Paraguay, but is also cultivated as a landscape plant in tropical, subtropical and warm temperate climates.

children.name: Philodendron biribiriense Sakur. & Mayo
children.description: Vulnerable (VU) D2. This species occurs in a restricted area and its populations are not known to be included in protected areas. It occurs on rock outcrops in ‘campo rupestre’, and this habitat is not under particular threat at the moment.

children.name: Philodendron blanchetianum Schott
children.description: Philodendron blanchetianum is a species of flowering plant in the arum family (Araceae) native to the Atlantic Forest of north-eastern and south-eastern Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron bogotense Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron bomboizense Croat & Cerón
children.description: Philodendron bomboizense is endemic to Ecuador, known only from the type locality in Morona-Santiago Province at 1700-1750 m elevation in Lower montane moist forest or Montane wet forest life zones.

children.name: Philodendron bonifaziae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron borgesii G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela: Dtto San Cristóbal, Edo Táchira.

children.name: Philodendron brandii Grayum
children.description: Known only by the type collection, from the Río Atrato basin of northwestern Colombia (Antioquia Department).

children.name: Philodendron brandtianum K.Krause
children.description: Philodendron brandtianum is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron.

children.name: Philodendron brantii Croat
children.description: Philodendron brantii is endemic to Colombia, known only from the type locality in the Department of Antioquia at 1850 m in a Tropical wet forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron breedlovei Croat
children.description: Known only from the type locality in Mexico (Chiapas). Since its type locality is very near Guatemala, it is expected to be found there as well.

children.name: Philodendron brenesii Standl.
children.description: Philodendron brenesii is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron brent-berlinii Croat
children.description: The species is characterized by deeply 3-lobed, yellowish gray-drying blades. It is closely related to P. ampamii, which shares similarly deeply 3-lobed blades with prominent lateral auricles. Philodendron ampamii differs in having blades drying dark brown above, dark yellow-brown below with the major veins drying broadly convex on lower surface. In addition, the spathe dries somewhat blackened w

children.name: Philodendron brevispathum Schott
children.description: Though long known only from the Caribbean coast of Panama, Philodendron brevispathum is now known to be a locally rare but more widespread species with special ecological requirements. It ranges from Nicaragua to Panama at 0--280 m with disjunct populations in South America, there ranging from Venezuela to Brazil (Amazonas), Colombia (Vichada, Meta), Ecuador (Napo), Peru (Loreto), and Bolivia, at elevations of 60 to 230 meters.

children.name: Philodendron brewsterense Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, where it is known only from the type specimen collected on Cerro Brewster in Comarca de San Blas Province.

children.name: Philodendron brunneicaule Croat & Grayum
children.description: Philodendron brunneicaule is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron bucayense Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron buntingianum Croat
children.description: Known only from Venezuela in the Cordillera de Merida ranging from Merida to Tachira.

children.name: Philodendron burgeri Grayum
children.description: Pacific slope from near the Río Grande de Tárcoles to the Golfo Dulce region in southwestern Costa Rica, and disjunctly on the Azuero Peninsula of central Panama.

children.name: Philodendron burle-marxii G.M.Barroso
children.description: Philodendron burle-marxii is a plant in the genus Philodendron native to South America ranging from Colombia to Ecuador and Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron calatheifolium G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela (Táchira), known only from the southern extreme of the Cordillera de Mérida at the headwaters of the Río Uribante basin, north of the Táchira depression.

children.name: Philodendron camarae Croat
children.description: Philodendron camarae is endemic to Colombia in the Department of Chocó at 100 m elevation in Tropical wet forest to Tropical rain forest transition area life zones.

children.name: Philodendron campii Croat
children.description: Philodendron campii is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, and to adjoining parts of Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron camposportoanum G.M.Barroso
children.description: Philodendron camposportoanum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron canaimae G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Bolívar). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron candamoense Croat
children.description: Philodendron candamoense is endemic to Peru, known only from the type locality in Puno Department at 790 m in a Subtropical rain forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron canicaule Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron canicaule must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although locally common in the area of the type locality, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia. It is possible that the species is more widespread than is currently known, because much of the Pacific slope is still poorly known.

children.name: Philodendron caracaraiense Croat
children.description: Philodendron caracaraiense is known only from Brazil but could be expected in southern Venezuela. It occurs on white sand soils in flooded campinas at about 200 m elevation probably in a Tropical moist forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron carajasense E.G.Gonç. & A.J.Arruda
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Pará). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron caranoense Croat, Edwin Trujillo & Marco Correa
children.description: Philodendron caranoense is endemic to Colombia, known only from the type locality on the eastern slopes of the Cordillera Oriental in Caqueta Department at 900 m elevation in a Lower montane rain forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron cardonii Croat
children.description: Philodendron cardonii is a member of P. subg. Philodendron, probably a member of sect. Macrobelium, but further classification is not possible without further studies. It is characterised by its elongated internodes, its narrowly ovate-elliptic leaves, which are truncate or sagittate at the base, have 12–15 pairs of primary lateral veins and 3–4 pairs of basal veins all free to the base, and its spathe, which is pale green outside and dark red-purple inside the lower part of the tube.

children.name: Philodendron cardosoi E.G.Gonç.
children.description: Brazil: Southeastern Pará and - probably - in the adjacent state of Tocantins, in central N Brazil, on quartzite outcrops.

children.name: Philodendron carinatum E.G.Gonç.
children.description: Philodendron carinatum is a flowering plant belonging to the genus Philodendron.

children.name: Philodendron cataniapoense G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela, Territorio Federal Amazonas.

children.name: Philodendron caudatum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Bolivia. It is a climbing shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron chimantae G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to S. Venezuela. It is a perennial or epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron chimboanum Engl.
children.description: Philodendron chimboanum is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron chinchamayense Engl.
children.description: Peru, Dep. Junin, Tarma Province, near La Merced in Chanchamoyo-Tal.

children.name: Philodendron chiriquense Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known from Bocas del Toro, Chiriquí and Coclé Provinces. It is frequent in the cloud forests near the Continental Divide in the Fortuna Dam area.

children.name: Philodendron chirripoense Croat & Grayum
children.description: The species is characterized by its scandent habit, very long and slender internodes (drying <3 mm diam.), slender petioles about as long as the small, narrowly ovate, subcordate blades, and especially by the inflorescence being longer than the petioles. Philodendron chirripoense is not similar to any other species in either Central or South America, but it might be confused with P. microstictum,

children.name: Philodendron chrysocarpum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron chrysocarpum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from both Chocó and Valle departments and is common in the Bajo Calima area.

children.name: Philodendron cipoense Sakur. & Mayo
children.description: Vulnerable (VU) D2. This species occurs in a restricted area and its populations are included within the Parque Nacional da Serra do Cipó. It occurs on rock outcrops in campo rupestre; this habitat is not under particular threat at the moment.

children.name: Philodendron clarkei Croat
children.description: It is characterized by its deciduous, usually 2-ribbed cataphylls, D-shaped to V-shaped petioles, more or less oblong blackish-drying blades with widely spaced primary lateral veins and its clusters of whitish spathes.

children.name: Philodendron clewellii Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known only from the Serranía de Pirre.

children.name: Philodendron colombianum R.E.Schult.
children.description: Colombia: Comisarías del Amazonas y Vaupés, Río Apaporis, Soratama (above mouth of Río Kananarí) and vicinity.

children.name: Philodendron coloradense Croat
children.description: It is characterized by having grayish internodes being longer than broad, green, unribbed, deciduous cataphylls, obtusely flattened petioles, ovate-cordate reddish brown-drying blades with a spathulate sinus and a weakly developed posterior rib which is barely or not at all naked, and paired, green inflorescences bent somewhat at the apex of the peduncule. The species is perhaps closest to P. grayumii, which differs in having 7--8 (versus 4--5)

children.name: Philodendron condorcanquense Croat
children.description: Characterized by hemiepiphytic scandent habit, closely ridged, yellow brown-drying stems, mostly fully sheathed petioles, and especially by its elliptic blades which dry grayish yellow-green below and have conspicuous minor veins on both surfaces, with conspicuous granular surfaces below. Philodendron condorcanquense is similar to P. exile in having narrowly ovate blades, less than 2.2 times lont

children.name: Philodendron conforme G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela: Amazonas, Depto Río Negro.

children.name: Philodendron consanguineum Schott
children.description: Philodendron consanguineum, the rascagarganta, is a flowering plant belonging to the genus Philodendron.

children.name: Philodendron consobrinum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Táchira). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron copense Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama (but should be expected in eastern Costa Rica) and is known from Bocas del Toro and Coclé (El Copé).

children.name: Philodendron cordatum Kunth ex Schott
children.description: Philodendron cordatum is an uncommon species not often found or offered as a houseplant.

children.name: Philodendron coriaceum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron coriaceum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since the species is widespread in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron correae Croat
children.description: Endemic to western Panama in Chiriquí and Bocas del Toro Provinces.

children.name: Philodendron cotapatense Croat & Acebey
children.description: It is characterized by its somewhat grayish drying, narrowly oblong-oblanceolate blades that lack any obvious primary lateral veins and its moderately small, narrowly pedunculate, blackish drying inflorescences. It is closest to P. paxianum K. Krause, which differs in having leaf blades with distinct primary lateral veins.

children.name: Philodendron cotobrusense Croat & Grayum
children.description: This species is characterized by its appressed-climbing habit, sharply two-ribbed, deciduous cataphylls, short, thick internodes with a silvery-gray epidermis, petioles about equaling the deeply three-lobed, closely veined blades (with more than 16 pairs of primary lateral veins), and especially by the inflorescences in clusters of up to five per leaf axil with the spathe tube green outside, red-violet within and the blade creamy yellow on outside and creamy white within.

children.name: Philodendron cotonense Croat & Grayum
children.description: Known only from eastern Costa Rica and western Panama.

children.name: Philodendron craspedodromum R.E.Schult.
children.description: Known from southern Venezuela (Amazonas) and southern Colombia (Vaupes) at 100-800 m. In Venezuela, it is known only from the Department of Atabapo at Cucurital de Caname and in the Serranfa Yutaje on the Río Manapiare.

children.name: Philodendron crassinervium Lindl.
children.description: Philodendron crassinervium is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to southeast Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron crassispathum Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from central Costa Rica to western Panama.

children.name: Philodendron crassum Rendle
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Rio de Janeiro). It grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron cremersii Croat & Grayum
children.description: Apparently endemic to French Guiana, known principally from the Montagnes de Kaw at 100-250 m. It is common along the road to Montagne Kaw east of Cayenne. It is also known from a single collection along the road between Cayenne and Regina.

children.name: Philodendron cretosum Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to Panama. The species is perhaps restricted to the Atlantic drainage but has been collected principally from areas along the Continental Divide in Panama.

children.name: Philodendron croatii Grayum
children.description: Spottily distributed in central and eastern Panama, with an aberrant population (provisionally included here) on the Colombian border.

children.name: Philodendron cruentospathum Madison
children.description: Philodendron cruentospathum is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron cruentum Poepp.
children.description: Philodendron cruentum, the redleaf, is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to Peru.

children.name: Philodendron cuneatum Engl.
children.description: Brazil (Acre, Amazonas), Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron curvilobum Schott
children.description: Near Threatened (NT), this species is scattered along a narrow strip of land near the coast, and such forests are under constant threat from land development. The populations in Rio de Janeiro are protected within the Parque Nacional da Serra da Tijuca.

children.name: Philodendron curvipetiolatum Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron daniellii Croat & Oberle
children.description: Philodendron danielii is known only from Colombia in Antioquia Department at 2,250-2,560 m elevation in areas of Lower montane moist forest (bh-MB).

children.name: Philodendron danteanum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is N. Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron davidneillii Croat
children.description: Philodendron davidneillii is apparently endemic to Ecuador, known only from the type locality in Orellana Province in the drainage of the Río Napo at 180 m elevation in a Tropical moist forest life zone. It is to be expected at least in adjacent Peru which lies relatively near the type locality.

children.name: Philodendron davidsei G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela: Dtto. Colón, Edo. Zulia.

children.name: Philodendron davidsonii Croat
children.description: Philodendron davidsonii is a flowering plant belonging to the genus Philodendron.

children.name: Philodendron deflexum Poepp. ex Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia, Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron delannayi Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron delascioi G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron delgadoae Croat & Delannay
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron delinksii Croat & Köster
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron deltoideum Poepp.
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru to W. Bolivia. It is a climbing epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron densivenium Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron devansayeanum André
children.description: Philodendron devansayeanum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron devianum Croat
children.description: It is apparently a member of Philodendron subg. Philodendron sect. Macrobelium subsect. Glossophyllum series Ovata and is characterised by its sharply flattened juvenile petioles, sharply D-shaped pre-adult petioles, obtusely flattened adult petioles, broadly ovate-cordate blades which are glossy above and matte below. It differs from most species in that section by the glossy upper surface of the leaf blades. Philodendron devianum is somewhat similar to P. merenbergense (also published in th

children.name: Philodendron dioscoreoides Gleason
children.description: The native range of this species is Guianas. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron discretivenium Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: Philodendron discretivenium is endemic to Colombia and is known only from the western slopes of the Cordillera Occidental, Valle Department.

children.name: Philodendron distantilobum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru to Bolivia and N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron divaricatum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Colombia to Bolivia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron dodsonii Croat & Grayum
children.description: Known from Costa Rica, Colombia, and Ecuador and it expected to be found on the Caribbean slope of Panama. In Costa Rica, it occurs at 240 to 1300 m elevation, principally on the Atlantic slope but also on the Pacific slope on the Fila Costeña in Tropical wet forest and especially in Premontane rain forest life zones. In Ecuador, this species is known from

children.name: Philodendron dolichophyllum Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama (though to be expected in eastern Costa Rica).

children.name: Philodendron dominicalense Croat & Grayum
children.description: Endemic to southwest Costa Rica on the Pacific slope in the vicinity of the type locality along San Isidro-Dominical road.

children.name: Philodendron dressleri G.S.Bunting
children.description: Endemic to west central Mexico from coastal Nayarit including Tres Marías Islands, off the western coast of Mexico) to southern Sinaloa.

children.name: Philodendron dryanderae Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron dryanderae must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is widespread on the Pacific slope of Colombia and common in the Bajo Calima area.

children.name: Philodendron duckei Croat & Grayum
children.description: Philodendron duckei is a plant species native to the French Guiana, Suriname and Brazil but cultivated as an ornamental elsewhere.

children.name: Philodendron dunstervilleorum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Venezuela to N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron dussii Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Dominica, Martinique. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron dwyeri Croat
children.description: Endemic to Belize, known only from the type collection in Cayo District of Belize at the Macal (Macaw) River near the Guacamallo Bridge.

children.name: Philodendron dyscarpium R.E.Schult.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to S. Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron eburneum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron ecordatum Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Guianas, N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron edenudatum Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama. It perhaps occurs in the adjacent Chocó of Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron edmundoi G.M.Barroso
children.description: Philodendron edmundoi is an endangered species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to southeastern Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron planadense Croat

children.name: Philodendron pogonocaule Madison

Philodendron pseudauriculatum is most easily confused with

children.name: Philodendron pseudoundulatum Grau

These are Foster 7732 (Peru, Pasco, Oxapampa), Asplund 18412 and Croat 58803 (Napo), Croat 99445 (Orellana), Croat 73480 (Pastaza) and (Napo).

children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Nicaragua to Panama. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rimachii Croat
children.description: Planta terrestris; internodia brevia, 1-1.5 cm diam.; cataphylla viridia, (5.5-)7-13.5 cm longa, decidua; petiolus 11-43 cm longus; lamina triangulari-ovato-subsagittata, 18-38 cm longa, 5-22 cm lata; lobulis posterioribus 2.5-12 cm longis, nervis primariis lateralibus 3-8 utroque; inflorescentia 1-2 per quoque axillam, pedunculo 6-10 cm longo; spatha (4-)5.2-7.5 cm longa, tubo viride, lamina alba; spadix 6.7 cm longus.

children.name: Philodendron rio-pretense C.A.S.Bat. & M.L.Soares
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (NE. Amazonas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron riparium Engl.
children.description: Philodendron riparium is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron robustum Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Trop. America (?). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rodrigueziae Croat & Grayum
children.description: Known definitely only from the vicinity of the private ENDESA Reserve, established by the Corporatión Forestal Juan Manuel Durini near the town of Pedro Vicente Maldonado, Pichincha Province, Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron roezlii W.Bull
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rojasianum Standl. & Steyerm.
children.description: Known from three disjunct regions: northern Chiapas (Mexico), Guatemala, and central Costa Rica.

children.name: Philodendron romeroi Grayum
children.description: Endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Cesar and Magdalena Departments, Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron roraimae K.Krause
children.description: Not easily confused with any other, though it has leaf blades and cataphylls somewhat like larger plants of Philodendron chimantae. However that species differs in having a petiole which is usually conspicuously winged-angled, at least on the adaxial surface.

children.name: Philodendron roseocataphyllum Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: Philodendron roseocataphyllum ranges along the Pacific slope of NW South America from Colombia (Choco) to Ecuador (Esmeraldas). At Cabo Corrientes it is occasional to common in the forest, usually occurring to 3 m high on trees.

children.name: Philodendron roseopetiolatum Nadruz & Mayo
children.description: Critically Endangered (CR), B1, a, b (i, iii); extent of occurence < 100 km 2. Only known from the type locality, where it was studied in the field by the first author. Subpopulations of this taxon are protected within the Reserva Ecológica de Macaé de Cima.

children.name: Philodendron roseospathum Croat
children.description: Ranges from Panama to Colombia. In Panama, this taxon is restricted to both sides of the Panama Canal, ranging from Veraguas to San Blas, mostly in Premontane rain forest or less frequently in Tropical wet forest life zones, at 350 to 1000 m elevation. In Colombia, it has been collected only in tropical pluvial forest at 100 to 900 meters.

children.name: Philodendron rothschuhianum  Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from Honduras (Gracias a Dios) and from Nicaragua (Río San Juan, Zelaya, Jinotega and Matagalpa) to Panama (Bocas del Toro, Veraguas, and Coclé), principally on the Atlantic slope.

children.name: Philodendron rubioi Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rubrocinctum Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rubromaculatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron rubromaculatum must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). There is no reason to assume that it is exceedingly rare because only a tiny fraction of the Bajo Calima region has been studied, but it has not been collected elsewhere from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron rudgeanum Schott
children.description: From Trinidad and northeastern Venezuela through the Guianas to northeastern Brazil (Amapá and Belém), then disjunctly to Bahia.

children.name: Philodendron rugapetiolatum Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rugosum Bogner & G.S.Bunting
children.description: Philodendron rugosum is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron ruizii Schott
children.description: Found along the western border of South America from the southwestern tip of Colombia (Putumayo), Ecuador (Azuay, Esmeraldas, Morona-Santiago, Napo, Pastaza, Zamora-Chinchipe), Peru (Amazonas, Cajamarca, Cusco, Huanuco, Junin, Pasco, San Martín), Bolivia (Cochabamba, La Paz.) This species is found on the eastern side of the Andes between 150–2300 m. In Ecuador, this plant is typically found above 1500 m and is found more commonly in Premontane wet forest and Montane wet forest. It is found le

children.name: Philodendron ruthianum Nadruz
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Espírito Santo). It is a climbing epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sabaletense Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sagittifolium Liebm.
children.description: Ranges from Mexico (Veracruz) to Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron samayense G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela (Bolívar: Dtto Roscio).

children.name: Philodendron sanmarcoense Croat
children.description: Philodendron sanmarcosense is known only from type locality in Carchi Province of Ecuador near the Colombian border at 740 m in a Premontane wet forest life zone. It is expected to be found in adjacent Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron santodominguense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is NW. Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron scalarinerve Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron scherberichii Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: Planta hemiepiphytica, ad 1.5 m; internodia 1.2-15 cm longa, 1.2-2.5 cm diam.; cataphylla ad 38 cm longa, debiliter 1-costata ad apex; petiolus (14-)30-40 cm longus, 3-7 mm diam., teres; geniculum ad 4 cm longum, 9 mm diam.; lamina anguste ovata-elliptica, (27-)45-60 cm longa, (9-)16.5-27 cm lata; nervis lateralibus (11-)17-21 utroque; inflorescentia solitaria pedunculo 3-3.5 cm longo; spatha 15.5-19.5 cm longa, 6 cm lata per anthesis, rubroviolacea vel marronina, sine constrictio; spadix pro

children.name: Philodendron schmidtiae Croat & Cerón
children.description: Philodendron schmidtiae is currently known only from Ecuador but it is to be expected in adjacent Colombia (Putumayo) and in Peru (Amazonas). In Ecuador it is known from Sucumbios, Napo, Pastaza, Morona-Santiago and Zamora-Chinchipe, ranging from 450-2400 m. An unidentified collection from Peru (A. Monteagudo et. al. 13658) from the Parque Nacional Yanachaga-Chemillén at 2361 m is very similar but has blades that are matte rather than semiglossy on the upper surface.

children.name: Philodendron schottianum H.Wendl. ex Schott
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to Panama. In Panama, this species ranges no further east than Veraguas (Cerro Tute), except for a disjunct occurrence on Cerro Jefe in Panama Province. All Costa Rican collections are from the northern slopes of the Cordillera Central in Alajue-la, Heredia, and San Jose, and the northern end of the Cordillera de Talamanca in the Tapanti region of Cartago Province. It is to be expected throughout much of the Cordillera de Talamanca.

children.name: Philodendron schottii K.Koch
children.description: Occurs on the island of Jamaica and on the mainland from southern Mexico to east-central Panama, thence distinctly to southwestern Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron scitulum G.S.Bunting
children.description: This species is totally distinct from P. auyantepuiense Bunt., differing by the proportionally broader leaf blade of thinner consistency with a few, more or less prominent, primary lateral veins. The latter species, known only from Auyantepui in the state of Bolivar, has a coriaceous (in vivo possibly somewhat fleshy) leaf blade with numerous, subequal lateral veins all manifest and a few primary

children.name: Philodendron scottmorianum Croat & Moonen
children.description: The conservation status for the species should be considered NT (Near threatened, IUCN 2001). Although the species is relatively common in the region where it was collected, it has not previously been collected in French Guiana or in adjacent countries.

children.name: Philodendron seguine Schott
children.description: Virtually endemic to Mexico where it ranges from central Veracruz to easternmost Chiapas. It has also been collected once in Guatemala.

children.name: Philodendron senatocarpium Madison
children.description: North coastal Ecuador, with a seemingly disjunct population on the western slope of the Colombian Cordillera Occidental in Antioquia and Chocó Departments.

children.name: Philodendron serpens Hook.f.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sharoniae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron silverstonei Croat
children.description: The species is a member of Philodendron subg. Philodendron sect. Macrobelium subsect. Glossophyllum series Ovata and is recognised by its hemiepiphytic habit, thick stem with short internodes, deciduous cataphylls, subterete petioles, its large matte, ovate-sagittate leaf blades with a well-developed posterior rib and 10–12 pairs of basal veins, as well as by up to 5 inflorescences per axil with long peduncles, the spathe tube green outside, red-violet inside and with the spathe blade green o

children.name: Philodendron simmondsii Mayo
children.description: Philodendron simmondsii is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, endemic to Trinidad.

children.name: Philodendron simonianum Sakur.
children.description: Critically Endangered (CR), B1, a, b (i, iii); extent of occurence < 100 km2. Only known from the type locality and its habitat is under pressure from deforestation, road building and agricultural and urban development. It has not been recorded in any protected area.

children.name: Philodendron simsii  Sweet ex Kunth
children.description: Trinidad, Tobago. Guyana, Lesser Antilles as far north as Virgin Islands.

children.name: Philodendron simulans G.S.Bunting
children.description: The retention of the old cataphylls easily distinguishes this species from P. acutatum. Also, the nervature is inconspicuous, drying darker brown than the ground color of the blade, and' the primary lateral veins arise at a sharper angle. In P. acutatum, the veins are conspicuous, drying much paler than the base color of the blade, and the primary lateral veins originate at a wide angle (70-80°).

children.name: Philodendron smithii Engl.
children.description: Ranges from Mexico (mostly in Chiapas, Tabasco, and Quintana Roo) to Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua on the Atlantic slope.

children.name: Philodendron sodiroi N.E.Br.
children.description: Philodendron sodiroi is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron sonderianum Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (S. Minas Gerais). It is a hemiepiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sousae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Mexico (Chiapas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sparreorum Croat
children.description: The species is recognized by its thick internodes, often longer than broad and drying with a smooth, light brown epidermis, as well as by its narrowly ovate-cordate blades with pale-drying major veins. More critical for recognition are the clusters of numerous, small, more or less pale orange inflorescences in one or more leaf axils, and especially the unusual pistils that have long, protruding, tapering styles.

children.name: Philodendron spec  K.Koch, 1855
children.description: Evergreen, small to gigantic, mostly climbing hemiepiphytes or epiphytes, sometimes arborescent to rhizomatous terrestrials; leaves with abundant resin canals; leaf blade very variable in shape, from linear to bipinnatifid, trisect or pedatisect, lacking a submarginal collective vein, fine venation parallel-pinnate; inflorescence secreting resin from spathe or spadix at anthesis; endothecium nearly always lacking cell wall thickenings; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; ovary usually 4-8-loc

children.name: Philodendron speciosum Schott, 1832
children.description: Philodendron speciosum, synonym Thaumatophyllum speciosum, is a species of plant in the family Araceae, native to Brazil and Bolivia.

children.name: Philodendron sphalerum Schott
children.description: Least Concern (LC). Although this species is not frequently collected, its distribution is widespread in Northern South America. In Brazil there are populations protected within the Reserva Ducke, Amazonas state.

children.name: Philodendron spiritus-sancti G.S.Bunting
children.description: Philodendron spiritus-sancti is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to the Brazilian state of Espírito Santo, which is the origin of its scientific name.

children.name: Philodendron splitgerberi Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Guianas, N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron spruceanum G.S.Bunting
children.description: Philodendron spruceanum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to southern Venezuela. It was first described by George Sydney Bunting in 1975.

children.name: Philodendron squamicaule Croat & Grayum
children.description: Philodendron squamicaule is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron squamiferum Poepp.
children.description: Philodendron squamiferum, known as Squamiferum for short, is a rare species of plant in the family Araceae, native to French Guiana, Suriname, and northern Brazil.

children.name: Philodendron squamipetiolatum Croat
children.description: Ranges from Panama to Ecuador. In Panama this species is known only from along the Continental Divide in Cocle Province, whereas in South America it occurs along the Pacific slope of the Andes.

children.name: Philodendron standleyi Grayum
children.description: Central Veracruz, Mexico, to Veraguas, Panama.

children.name: Philodendron stenophyllum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron steyermarkii G.S.Bunting
children.description: The species is distinguished by its high climbing habit, long, slender internodes, terete petioles, the ovate-oblong blades with scarcely any development of primary lateral veins and with a sub-cordate base. The inflorescence is creamy, suffused with lilac outside on the tube and purple-magenta inside on the tube. Herbarium material is perhaps most easily confused with P. ptarianum, but the latter differs in having short internodes, a creeping

children.name: Philodendron straminicaule Croat
children.description: Known only from the Cordillera de Guanacaste in northwest Costa Rica and in western Panama, from Chiriqui and Bocas del Toro to Coclé Province.

children.name: Philodendron striatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron striatum must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although locally common in the Bajo Calima region, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron strictum G.S.Bunting
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to western Panama, Venezuela (Tachira), Colombia (Antioquia, Choco), and Ecuador (Carchi, Esrneraldas). In Costa Rica, this species occurs at 850 to 1525 m, and in Panama at 680 to 1665 m elevation in Lower Montane rain. Premontane rain, and Tropical wet forest life zones. In Colombia, this species has been collected at 100 to 150 m in Choco and Valle Departments, and in An

children.name: Philodendron suberosum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron suberosum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from six collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments and many separate localities.

children.name: Philodendron subhastatum K.Krause
children.description: Ranges along the Pacific slope and adjacent lowlands of Colombia and Ecuador to the Provincias of Guayas and Chimborazo. In the Cabo Corrientes region it was collected from a semi-open area on the banks of Río Arusicito.

children.name: Philodendron subincisum Schott
children.description: Endemic to Mexico, known only from northern Veracruz in the Poza Rica region.

children.name: Philodendron sucrense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Sucre). It is a epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sulcatum K.Krause
children.description: North-central Nicaragua through Costa Rica and Panama, thence discontinuously along the Pacific slope of South America south to Guayas and Chimborazo Provinces, Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron sulcicaule Croat
children.description: Ranges from extreme southeastern Costa Rica to the Atlantic slope of Panama.

children.name: Philodendron surinamense  Engl.
children.description: Ranges from southern Venezuela (Bolívar and Amazonas) and the Guianas to Ecuador (Pastaza), Peru (Loreto), and Brazil (Amapá, Roraima, Amazonas, Maranhâo, and Bahia).

children.name: Philodendron swartiae Croat
children.description: The species is recognized by terrestrial habit, creeping stems, persistent cataphyll fibers, densely warty-verrucose-scaly petioles, and ovate-cordate blades. Philodendron swartiae is related to other members in an unnamed section and species in the group include P. pastazanum K. Krause and P. gloriosum André.

children.name: Philodendron tachirense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The species is recognized by its scandent habit, caducous, unribbed cataphyll, moderately spongy, more or less terete petioles, its ovate, inequi-laterally ovate, subcordate to cordate blades with a triangular sinus which is broader than deep and with the posterior rib not naked. Also characteristic are the inflorescences which occur in clusters of 4-5 per axil, have uncon-stricted spathes with the tubes green outside, maroon within and with the blades white on both surfaces.

children.name: Philodendron tarmense Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tenuipes Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tenuispadix E.G.Gonç.
children.description: Critically Endangered (CR), B1, a, b (i, iii); extent of occurence < 100 km 2, this species occurs in two populations in Espírito Santo, in a region where the destruction of the original vegetation is comprehensive. One population is protected within the Reserva Biológica Santa Lúcia, and specimens are cultivated at Sítio Roberto Burle-Marx, in Rio de Janeiro.

children.name: Philodendron teretipes Sprague
children.description: Affinities with Philodendron glaziovii Hook. f., distinguished from this by terete petioles, smaller subsessile inflorescence and fewer ovules.

children.name: Philodendron thalassicum Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from central Costa Rica to western Panama (Chiriquí).

children.name: Philodendron thaliifolium Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron theofiloanum Calazans
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Minas Gerais). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tortum M.L.Soares & Mayo
children.description: Philodendron tortum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to northern Brazil and Bolivia.

children.name: Philodendron toshibae M.L.Soares & Mayo
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron traunii Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron triangulare G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Trujillo). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tricostatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron tricostatum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from six collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments and many separate localities.

children.name: Philodendron triplum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Bolívar). It is a epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron trojitense Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron trojitense must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although reasonably common in the area of the type locality, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia. It is possible that the species is more widespread than is currently known because much of the Pacific slope is still poorly known.

children.name: Philodendron trujilloi G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tuerckheimii Grayum
children.description: North-central Oaxaca and east-central Veracruz to extreme eastern Panama, south through the Colombian Cordillera Occidental to northwestern Ecuador, and east through the Colombian Cordilleras Central and Oriental and the Venezuelan Cordillera de Merida to the western end of the Cordillera de la Costa in Yaracuy State.

children.name: Philodendron tysonii Croat
children.description: Known only from Panama, but is expected to be found in the Cordillera de Talamanca of Costa Rica.

children.name: Philodendron ubigantupense Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known only from the type locality along the Atlantic coast.

children.name: Philodendron uleanum Engl.
children.description: Least Concern (LC). Although this species is not frequently collected, its distribution is widespread in Northern and Northwestern South America. The populations do not seem to be included in conservation areas so far.

children.name: Philodendron urraoense Croat
children.description: Philodendron urraoense is a member of P. sect. Philodendron sect. Macrobelium subsect. Macrobelium and is characterised by its hemiepiphytic climbing habit, the internodes usually longer than broad and drying yellow-brown with longitudinal ridges, petioles subterete and shorter than blades and drying blackened, blades ovatecordate and drying somewhat blackened with a narrow, triangular sinus and with the basal veins free to the base or nearly so as well as by the cluster of up to 8 moderately

children.name: Philodendron ushanum Croat & Moonen
children.description: Planta hemiepiphytica; internodia adulta 3.5-6.5(-8) cm longa, 8-10 mm diam.; cataphylla 13-18 cm longa, 2-costata, persistentia semi-intacta; petiolus subteres, 17-19 cm longus, 1-1.3 cm diam.; lamina anguste ovata, 24-27 cm longa, 9-10 cm lata, nervis primariis lateralibus 4-6 utroque; inflorescentia solitaria, pedunculo 1.5-2 cm longo; spatha 10.5 cm longa, tubo 4.5-5 cm longo, 2 cm diam.; spadix 9 cm longus, parte pistillata 2.7 cm longa, 1.2 cm diam., pistillis 5-6-locularibus, ovulis 3-

children.name: Philodendron utleyanum Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known only by the type specimen from Colón Province.

children.name: Philodendron validinervium Engl.
children.description: Philodendron validinervium is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron vargealtense Sakur.
children.description: Philodendron vargealtense is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to southeastern Brazil in the state of Espírito Santo.

children.name: Philodendron variifolium Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron venosum  Croat
children.description: Spottily distributed in the coastal ranges of Venezuela to Trinidad (Northern Range) and Tobago, and possibly Barbados.

children.name: Philodendron ventricosum Madison
children.description: Philodendron ventricosum is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron venulosum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: Conservation for Philodendron venulosum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from six collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments and many separate localities.

children.name: Philodendron venustifoliatum E.G.Gonç. & Mayo
children.description: Brazil: so far known only from Distrito Federal and Goiás states.

children.name: Philodendron venustum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Colombia to S. Venezuela and Peru. It is a epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron verapazense Croat
children.description: Ranges from southern Mexico (Chiapas) to Guatemala (Alta Verapaz).

children.name: Philodendron verrucapetiolum Croat
children.description: Philodendron verrucapetiolum ranges from Colombia (Narino) to adjacent Ecuador (Carchi), at 1,780-2,010 m in Premontane wetforest. At La Planada, this species is apparently relatively frequent and widespread, having been collected near the summit of the hill above La Posada in the small patch of forest between the two pastured areas, along the trail to El Hondon beginning at Quebrade EI Tejon, in virgin cloud forest along Sendero La Vieja, and along the trail to the summit of the hill behind

children.name: Philodendron verrucosum L.Mathieu ex Schott
children.description: Philodendron verrucosum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron victoriae G.S.Bunting
children.description: Greatest affinity to P. barrosoanum but plant usually bigger, anterior lobe of the leaf blade narrower in proportion but less contracted in the lower part, lateral lobes more obtuse towards the apex, apex itself not attenuating, but obtuse-rounded, separated by a sinus which is more deep in proportion, spathe often shorter than the spadix and without an apical acumen.

children.name: Philodendron vinaceum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The species is a rosulate epiphytic herb characterized by its short internodes, a rotten mass of cataphylls (unribbed when fresh with the outer epidermis persisting for a time), its broadly ovate, usually moderately thick blades, which are rounded to subcordate at the base and brownish maroon when young on the lower surface. The petioles are generally somewhat shorter than the blades and are obtusely D-shaped to broadly sulcate adaxially, with usually prominent margins. The inflorescences are

children.name: Philodendron viride Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron wadedavisii Croat
children.description: Planta hemiepiphytica; internodia 1-2 cm longa, 5-8 mm diam.; cataphylla 6-10 cm longa, decidua; petiolus 7-9 cm longus; lamina anguste elliptica vel anguste obovato-elliptica, 28-40.5 cm longa, 8.5-10 cm lata, nervis primariis lateralibus 8-9 utroque; inflorescentia 1-2 per quoque axillam, pedunculo 3.5-4.5 cm longo; spatha 6.3-6.6 cm longa, 1-1.5 cm diam., viridis; spadix 5.3 cm longus.

children.name: Philodendron wallisii Regel ex Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron weberbaueri Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron wendlandii Schott

children.name: Philodendron werkhoveniae Croat
children.description: Occurs in Suriname and French Guiana. In French Guiana, it is known only from Haut Oyapock, Mt. St. Marcel, at 300-450 m elevation, along Crique Poivre.

children.name: Philodendron werneri Croat
children.description: Philodendron werneri is endemic to Ecuador, known only from the type locality in Zamora-Chinchipe Province at 2000 m in a Premontane moist forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron wilburii Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from northern Costa Rica to the Canal Area of Panama.

children.name: Philodendron wittianum Engl.
children.description: Least Concern (LC). Distributed throughout Northwestern South America, this species is not particularly threatened and some of its populations are included in protected areas.

children.name: Philodendron woronowii K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia (Antioquia). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron wullschlaegelii Schott

children.name: Philodendron wurdackii G.S.Bunting
children.description: Ranges throughout the northern Amazon region, extending from southern Venezuela, northern Brazil (Amazonas, Rio Japura, Rio Demeny) to southern Colombia (Vaupes, Meta), Ecuador (Napo and Pastaza) to Peru (Loreto) and occurs at 120-1,130 m. In Venezuela, it is known only from Amazonas (Rio Yatua, San Carlos de Rio Negro and base of Cerro Neblina).

children.name: Philodendron yavitense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Amazonas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron yutajense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Amazonas). It is a subshrub or shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Thaumatophyllum bipinnatifidum  Sakur., Calazans & Mayo

The species is native to South America, namely to Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, and Paraguay, but is also cultivated as a landscape plant in tropical, subtropical and warm temperate climates.

children.description: Philodendron xanadu, synonym Thaumatophyllum xanadu, is a perennial plant belonging to the arum family Araceae. It is native to south Brazil and Paraguay, but is widely cultivated as a landscape plant in tropical, subtropical, and warm temperate climates.

children.name: Zomicarpella amazonica Bogner
children.description: The genus Zomicarpella is more closely related to the genus Zomicarpa. Both have flat connectives of the male flowers, seeds with endosperm and a swollen funicle which is usually connected with the seed at maturity and breaks off at the placenta; Pilarum and Ulearum have seeds without endosperm. The pollen grains of the Zomicarpeae are similar: spherical, inaperturate and the exine is spinose, but there is a great difference in having sporopollenin in the genera Zomicarpa and Zomicarpella whi

children.name: Zomicarpella maculata N.E.Br.
children.description: COLOMBIA: without exact locality, introduced and cultivated in Belgium by J. Linden, Linden s. n. (K, holotype). PERU: Dept. Cuzco, Provo Cuzco, Distr. Camisea, Campamento San Martin C, Camisea Production Unit, west of camp, 467 m; 11°47'08"S, 72°41'57"W. Primary, moist lowland non-flooded forest dominated by bamboo (Guadua). Wet season. children.name: Hapaline
children.description: Hapaline — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Hapaline appendiculata Ridl.
children.description: Hapaline appendiculata differs from H. celatrix P.C.Boyce (Brunei) by its seasonally dormant habit, thinly coriaceous leaves and greatly elongated sterile appendix.

children.name: Hapaline benthamiana Schott
children.description: Myanmar (type), Thailand, Laos, and Vietnam.

children.name: Hapaline brownii Hook.f.
children.description: Native from southern Thailand to West Malesia. In Malesia: Malay Peninsula.

children.name: Hapaline celatrix P.C.Boyce
children.description: Malesia: endemic to Borneo: Sarawak & Brunei.

children.name: Hapaline colaniae Gagnep.
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Thailand, Vietnam. It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Hapaline ellipticifolia C.Y.Wu & H.Li
children.description: The native range of this species is China (SE. Yunnan) to Vietnam. It is a rhizomatous geophyte and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Hapaline kerrii Gagnep.
children.description: The native range of this species is Thailand. It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Hapaline kimthoae K.Z.Hein, Vuong & V.C.Nguyen
children.description: The native range of this species is Vietnam. It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Hapaline locii V.D.Nguyen & Croat
children.description: Herbaceous plant 15-25 cm tall. STEM tuberous-rhizomatous, 1.5-2 x 0.4-0.5 cm. LEAVES 2-3; lamina entire, elliptic to lanceolate, sometime ovate, 7-14 x 3.5-7 cm, base rounded to cordate or with triangular lobes directed outward in the form of a "V", sometime overlapping in juvenile phase, rarely parallel, apex acute to cuspidate, (acumen 7-12 mm long); primary lateral veins 3, angled from midrib at an angle of 60-90", collective veins 3-7 mm from the margin, the minor veins conspicuous; peti

children.description: Croatiella — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Stylochaeton
children.description: Stylochaeton — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Stylochaeton angolensis Engl.
children.description: Stigma oblique, shield-like; filaments of the stamens shorter than the anthers.

children.name: Stylochaeton bogneri Mayo
children.description: A distinctive species with stoloniferous rhizomes, named for Josef Bogner (München Botanic Garden) on whose excellent collections the description is primarily based. Leaf usually sagittate, basal half of blade margin convex, blade sometimes with grey-green patches between main veins; rhizome elongated, slender, up to 0.6 cm in diameter.

children.name: Stylochaeton borumensis N.E.Br.
children.description: Stigma discoid; filaments of the stamens clavate, longer than the anthers. This species is remarkable for the very thick clavate filaments of the stamens.

children.name: Stylochaeton crassispathum Bogner
children.description: Petiole-sheath broadly auriculate to rounded at apex; leaf-blade cordate-sagittate.

children.name: Stylochaeton cuculliferum Peter
children.description: Petiole-bases with distinct, transverse, maroon-purple, ridged barring; leaf-blade deeply sagittate, basal lobes subequal to median lobe.

children.name: Stylochaeton euryphyllum Mildbr.
children.description: Leaves appressed to soil-surface, subcircular and very shortly cordate with overlapping basal lobes; venation usually distinctly paler than rest of blade.

children.name: Stylochaeton grande N.E.Br.
children.description: The native range of this species is N. Somalia. It is a rhizomatous geophyte and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Stylochaeton grandis N.E.Br.
children.description: Inflorescence appearing before the leaves; spathe about 4 in. long; male perianth 3-lobed.

children.name: Stylochaeton hypogaeum Lepr.
children.description: Inflorescence and leaves present at the same time; spathe 2 inches long.

children.name: Stylochaeton kerensis N.E.Br.
children.description: S. kerensis has sometimes been confused with the W African S. hjpogaeus Lepr. (1834) which has narrower leaves, is usually taller and has a shorter spadix compared to the spathe. Ovary adnate to the perianth. Lateral leaf lobes 2.5-3.5 cm long, separated by an oblong to wide sinus.

children.name: Stylochaeton kornasii Malaisse & Bamps
children.description: Southeast Democratic Republic of Congo.

children.name: Stylochaeton lancifolium Kotschy & Peyr.
children.description: Leaves appearing after flowers; blade hastate with posterior lobes over 2 cm long, in savanna.

children.name: Stylochaeton malaissei Bogner
children.description: Petioli longi in parte inferiore maculati; lamina foliorum lanceolata, basi cuneata, apica acuta; baccae depresse globulatae; semina ellipsoidea, testa costata atrobrunnea, endospermio laete albo, embryone parvo. Stylochaeton malaissei differt a S. shabaensis laminis foliorum basi cuneatis; in S. shabaensis in contrario basi truncatis vel cordatis.

children.name: Stylochaeton milneanum Mayo
children.description: S. milneanus is closely related to S. salaamicus, differing mainly in shoot and cataphyll morphology. Terminal projection of cataphyll stipitate and sagittate; petiole-sheath short, inconspicuous, enclosed within cataphylls; leaf-pubescence ± sparse with weak hairs.

children.name: Stylochaeton natalensis Schott
children.description: A very variable species requiring further field studies. Old cataphylls and petiole-bases persisting around shoot-base forming conspicuous net-fibrous mass.

children.name: Stylochaeton oligocarpum Riedl
children.description: Though the male inflorescence and flowers are not known, the vegetative characters are so remarkable that the species can easily be recognised and is quite distinct also from species outside the Flora area. Lateral lobes of leaves 7-12 cm long, horizontally spreading.

children.name: Stylochaeton pilosum Bogner
children.description: Lamina foliorum rotunda vel subrotunda (5 – 7 × 4 –5.5 cm), supra glabra, subtus pilosa, apice cuspidata; spatha basi latior ad apicem versus constanter attenuata non constricta, apertura lateralis rimiformis; perigonium florum feminorum urceolatum, perigonium florum masculorum humile patelliforme. Stylochaeton zenkeri differt a S. pilosus laminis foliorum ovatis vel ellipticis (7.5 – 20 × 4 – 11 cm) totis glabris.

children.name: Stylochaeton puberulum N.E.Br.
children.description: The puberulous leaves and ovaries distinguish this from all the other species of the genus.

children.name: Stylochaeton salaamicum N.E.Br.
children.description: Leaves broadly hastate, greyish beneath, from being densely covered with minute black dots; veins dark

children.name: Stylochaeton shabaensis Malaisse & Bamps
children.description: Spathe subcylindric, leaf blade ovate, truncate to broadly cordate at the base, 15-24 x 8-18 cm; petiole entirely smooth, male and female zones of the spadix separated by a 2-3 mm long sterile zone. Ovary 3-6-ovulate.

children.name: Stylochaeton zenkeri Engl.
children.description: Leaves oblong, subacute, slightly obtuse at the base; spathe about 3 in. long Allied to S. lancifolius , Kotschy, according to Engler, who does not state if the leaves appear with or after the flowers; but as specimens of S. gabonicus, N. E. Br., have been distributed from Berlin under the name of S. Zenkeri (with the description of which they do not agree), it is assumed in the key to the species that S. Zenkeri somewhat resembles S. gabonicus

children.name: Anubias gilletii De Wild. & T.Durand
children.description: Anubias gilletii is a plant that was first described scientifically in 1901 by Émile Auguste Joseph De Wildeman and Th.

children.name: Anubias gracilis A.Chev. ex Hutch.

children.name: Cyrtosperma
children.description: Cyrtosperma — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Cyrtosperma beccarianum A.Hay
children.description: Lamina held with the posterior lobes up, anterior lobe down; spathe ovate to ovate-lanceolate.

children.name: Cyrtosperma bougainvillense A.Hay
children.description: Spathe deflected from and at least 1.5 times as long as the spadix; spadix glaucous; receptive stigmas red; seed stony, helically twisted. Bougainville Island.

children.name: Cyrtosperma brassii A.Hay
children.description: Flowers tetramerous. Spathe erect; leaves asperous in dry state. Rossel Island.

children.name: Cyrtosperma carrii A.Hay
children.description: The native range of this species is Papua New Guinea. It is a rhizomatous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Cyrtosperma cuspidispathum Alderw.
children.description: Lamina unarmed; lower part of spathe convolute.

children.name: Cyrtosperma giganteum Engl.
children.description: Ovary multiovulate; fruit up to 5-seeded; infructescence massive, to c. 35 cm long and c. 11 cm thick. Lorentz river in Irian Jaya.

children.name: Cyrtosperma gressittiorum A.Hay
children.description: Spathe hood-forming; leaves not asperous in the dry state. Sudest (= Tagula) Island.

children.name: Cyrtosperma hambalii A.Dearden & A.Hay
children.description: This species very closely resembles the rheophytic Cyrtosperma beccarianum in the shape of its leaves, differing in the short petioles. It differs further from that species in the extremely elongate dark greenish brown spathe, hexamerous flowers and exserted stamens. The spathe of C. beccarianum is ovate, wide open and generally white, the flowers are tetramerous and the stamens are not exserted at male anthesis. The very long spathe recalls that of C. cuspidispathum

children.name: Cyrtosperma johnstonii  N.E.Br.
children.description: Stamens exserted from the tepals at male anthesis; flowers hexamerous; Petioles and undersides of laminae with reddish-brown blotches; juvenile leaves with pink costae.

children.name: Cyrtosperma kokodense A.Hay
children.description: Lamina armed; lower part of spathe not convolute.

children.name: Cyrtosperma macrotum Becc. ex Engl.
children.description: Lamina held horizontally or with the posterior lobes down and anterior lobe up, or (rarely) all lobes slightly above horizontal; spathe narrowly lanceolate.

children.name: Cyrtosperma merkusii  Schott
children.description: Cyrtosperma merkusii or giant swamp taro, is a crop grown throughout Oceania and into South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Cyrtosperma timikense Imran & A.Hay
children.description: The native range of this species is W. New Guinea. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

Tuber dark outside, white inside, depressed globose, 0.5–3 × 0.5–3cm; new roots and buds appearing at apex in Apr–May; stolons much branched, spreading, pendulous, sometimes simple and creeping; bulbils numerous, smaller. Cataphylls white, lanceolate, ca. 9cm, membranous, convolute around both leaf and flower buds. children.name: Remusatia pumila  H.Li & A.Hay
children.description: Tuber yellowish brown outside, globose, 1–2.5cm in diam.; bulbiferous stolons spreading, creeping, slender, branched; bulbils many, covered by brown scales; bristles filiform, hooked. children.name: Pothos thomsonianus Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is SW. India. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Pothos tirunelveliensis Sasikala & Reema Kumari

children.description: Dracunculus vulgaris is a species of aroid flowering plant in the genus Dracunculus and the arum family Araceae. Common names include the common dracunculus, dragon lily, dragon arum, black arum and vampire lily.

children.description: Arum euxinum is a plant of the arum family (Araceae).

children.name: Arum gratum Schott
children.description: Plant small. Inflorescences borne at ground level. Pale purple washed spathe-limb, bicoloured spathe-tube interior. Spadix less than ? as long as the spathe-limb, stoutly clavate. Odour sweet-oily.

children.name: Arum hainesii Riedl
children.description: Inflorescence borne beneath the leaves. Spathe pale green on both surfaces. Spadix less than ½ as long as the spathe-limb, with numerous densely arranged staminodes; appendix stout, stipitate, pale brown.

children.name: Arum jacquemontii Blume
children.description: Inflorescence borne above leaves. Petioles dull purple. Spathe-limb interior purple. Spadix ? - ¾ as long as the spathe-limb; staminodes and pistillodes with long flexuous bristles and purple bases ; spadix-appendix cylindric, tapering basally. Inflorescence scentless. (similar to Arum korolkowii and Arum rupicola)

children.name: Arum lucanum Cavara & Grande
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Italy, Albania. It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Arum megobrebi Lobin, M.Neumann, Bogner & P.C.Boyce

children.name: Arum orientale M.Bieb.
children.description: Arum orientale is a woodland plant species of the family Araceae.

children.name: Arum palaestinum Boiss.
children.description: Arum palaestinum is a species of flowering herbaceous perennial plant in the genus Arum and the family Araceae.

children.name: Arum rupicola Boiss.

children.description: Arisaema triphyllum, the Jack-in-the-pulpit, is a species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae. It is a member of the Arisaema triphyllum complex, a group of four or five closely related taxa in eastern North America.

children.description: Dracontium guianense is very similar to D. polyphyllum, but differs in having a much longer peduncle (more than 30 cm above ground level).

children.name: Dracontium iquitense E.C.Morgan & J.A.Sperling
children.description: Terrestrial plant; tuber hemispherical, flat above and rounded below. Light tan throughout. Top of tuber collected less than 1cm under soil. Tubercles common throughout top surface of the tuber. Cataphylls 1-2 15-20cm long, purple in color. Leaves 1-2 with the petioles 100-150cm in length and 3-5cm diameter for the primary leaf and an occasional secondary leaf usually 1/2 to 2/3 in size. children.name: Dracontium laetum E.G.Gonç. & S.P.Santos
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Dracontium longipes Engl.
children.description: Dracontium longipes is easily confused vegetatively with D. plowmanii and D. spruceanum, but is distinguished from those species by having a cymbiform rather than an erect or arching spathe. Dracontium plowmanii also differs from D. longipes in having a spathe with undulate or lobed margins and small seeds with a single continuous ridge. children.description: Dracontium margaretae is an atypical member of the genus, recognized by its linear blade segments and by occurring in seasonally swampy habitats. Other distinguishing features include the linear or trifid juvenile leaf blades and tubercles borne at the apex and sides of the tuber. It is confused with no other species. This species grows well as an aquatic in cultivation.

children.name: Dracontium narae E.G.Gonç.
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Roraima). It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.description: Dracontium peruvianum has the longest leaves of any species in the genus, up to 6m long. The inflorescences of this species are superficially similar to those of D. pittieri, but are distinct by the more elongate fruiting spadix (to 23-35cm long vs. 10-20cm long for D. pittieri), more strongly ridged seeds (vs. less ridging in D. pittieri), and basal leaf segments that usually are free from the rachis. children.name: Dracontium pittieri Engl.
children.description: Dracontium pittieri is a species of flowering plant native to Costa Rica.

children.name: Dracontium plowmanii G.H.Zhu & Croat

It is easily confused with D. spruceanum, which differs in having larger seeds to 0.7 cm long, with three dorsal ridges, and usually entire and non-wavy spathe margins. children.name: Dracontium polyphyllum L.
children.description: Dracontium polyphyllum is distinguished by its often subterranean peduncle, usually broadly opened spathe with a glossy inner surface, and smooth, laterally convex seeds. Historically, it has been confused with D. asperum (see discussion of D. asperum). It is also similar to D. guianense, which differs in having the above-ground portion of the peduncle much longer than the spathe. children.name: Dracontium purdieanum  Engl.

children.name: Dracontium soconuscum Matuda
children.description: Dracontium soconuscum is easily confused vegetatively with D. grayumianum, but that species differs in having seeds with five or six strongly interrupted dorsal ridges, whereas D. soconuscum has seeds with three obvious and continuous dorsal ridges.

children.name: Dracontium ulei K.Krause

It is easily confused with D. bogneri, which shares a cucullate spathe covered inside with translucent scales. It differs in the leaves with more numerous more spreading primary veins, the larger inflorescence with a much broader lower spathe and female zone of the spadix, a short but nevertheless much longer appendix and the stamens with the connective rather dilated, spreading the thecae apart.

children.description: Schismatoglottis ridleyana represents a usually robust form with dull green broad leaves with rather prominent and closely spaced primary lateral veins and a fine dense velvety indumentum on the petioles and abaxial midrib.

children.name: Apoballis ovata  S.Y.Wong & P.C.Boyce
children.description: It differs in having rough internodes and puberulous, longer petioles, and interpistillar staminodes confined to each end of the female zone.
